Column formats for reactable

Source: R/html-widgets.R
phw_reactable_columns.Rd

Ready-made reactable::colDef()s for common PHW table columns. Pass them in columns = list(...) of phw_reactable() or reactable::reactable().

Usage

phw_col_bar(
  data,
  column,
  colour = phw_colours[["light_teal"]],
  digits = 0,
  ...
)

phw_col_heat(data, column, palette = "teals", domain = NULL, digits = 1, ...)

phw_col_rag(
  breaks,
  higher_is_better = TRUE,
  rag_palette = "rag_accessible",
  digits = 1,
  ...
)

phw_col_number(digits = 0, ...)

phw_col_percent(digits = 1, ...)

Arguments

data

The data frame (bar and heat columns need it to find the range).

column

The column, unquoted as in dplyr. A string works too.

colour

Bar colour.

digits

Decimal places.

...

Other reactable::colDef() arguments, e.g. name.

palette

Palette name or vector of colours.

domain

Range for the heat colours. Defaults to the column range.

breaks, higher_is_better

See phw_flextable_heat().

rag_palette

"rag" or "rag_accessible".

Value

A reactable::colDef().

Details

  • phw_col_bar(): the value with a horizontal bar behind it, scaled to the column's largest value. Good for counts and rates.

  • phw_col_heat(): cell background from a sequential or diverging palette, with readable text.

  • phw_col_rag(): red, amber or green cells with a shape, so status doesn't rely on colour alone.

  • phw_col_number() and phw_col_percent(): thousands separators and fixed decimals.

Examples

if (requireNamespace("reactable", quietly = TRUE)) {
  df <- data.frame(area = paste("Area", LETTERS[1:5]), cases = c(120, 85, 64, 19, 23),
                   rate = c(4.1, 2.2, 6.3, 1.0, 2.5), share = c(.38, .27, .2, .06, .07))
  phw_reactable(df, columns = list(
    cases = phw_col_bar(df, cases, name = "Cases"),
    rate = phw_col_heat(df, rate, name = "Rate"),
    share = phw_col_percent(name = "Share")
  ))
}
